picks.why: Refiners are the cleanest expression of the Hormuz and Sheskharis supply shock: record cracks (3-2-1 near $70, diesel above $90) and a ~$6 Brent-WTI spread flow straight to Valero, whose +38.9% 12-week trend is the strongest on the sheet and whose estimates the sell-side is still chasing.

The highest-beta large-cap crude play on escalating supply news (tanker attacks, stalled U.S.-Iran talks, the pressure campaign being readied), up 7.8% on the week with positive 4- and 12-week trends and about 13% headroom to its mean target.

The defense leg of the industrials call: the Iran escalation plays directly to PAC-3 missile defense, a +19.6% four-week trend backed by the up-to-$53.9B PAC-3 MSE framework and a fresh MDA award, and low beta in case Jackson Hole goes badly.

The direct play on the tech call's Aug 26 countdown: flat on the week (+0.5%) while memory and AMD ran, 4.8% below its high, and SMCI, TSMC and CoreWeave just re-confirmed AI capex; it also offsets the book if the oil premium drains.
The healthcare leg's single-name upside: +18.7% over four weeks and 2.2% below its all-time high going into the ~Aug 19 garetosmab decision, with little exposure to oil or the consumer.

summary: Energy is the lead call, so it gets two picks split between product cracks (VLO) and crude beta (COP), and LMT adds a defense leg on the same Iran escalation. NVDA and REGN hedge the book against the oil premium draining or a patient Warsh sparking a growth rally; I passed on BTC (-17% over 12 weeks) and GLD (little edge over SPY into Jackson Hole).
